## Python state survives file changes and restarts

The Python `code` tool now saves interpreter checkpoints between calls. It no longer reconstructs variables by rerunning earlier snippets. This fixes stale assertions after file edits, repeated tool operations, and old results being reused for new requests. Approval pauses resume from the saved execution point.

## Upgrade

Run `pitty upgrade`, then start PiTTy again.

**Existing Python state needs one explicit reset.** Old replay snapshots do not contain enough information for safe migration. The `code` tool returns a clear error asking for `reset=true` and preserves the original snapshot until reset. Reset clears Python variables and reloads saved tools. Conversation history and workspace files remain intact.

A material change to helper type signatures or execution limits also requires reset so a restored state cannot use stale contracts.

The interpreter update is pinned and installed inside PiTTy's private runtime. Global Pi, interpreter packages, settings, and session files are not rewritten by the installer. If dependency preparation fails, the previous runtime remains intact. Installation also handles symlinked paths, including macOS temporary folders.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/mistrjirka/PiTTy/compare/v0.7.10...v0.7.11)
